statement.text:
Let φ be an automorphism of prime order p of a finite group G such that
CG (φ) ⩽ Z(G).
    a) Is G soluble if p = 3? V. D. Mazurov and T. L. Nedorezov proved in (Algebra
and Logic, 35, no. 6 (1996), 392–397) that the group G is soluble for p = 2, and there
are examples of unsoluble G for all p > 3.
    b) If G is soluble, is the derived length of G bounded in terms of p?
    c) (V. K. Kharchenko). If G is a p-group, is the derived length of G bounded in
terms of p? (V. V. Bludov produced a simple example showing that the nilpotency
class cannot be bounded.)                                                E. I. Khukhro
